[quote=oceanice_republic;59857331][i][b]Night March[/b]

[u]S.S.E. order[/u]

The S.S.E. Secret Sereckist Enforce has deployed to deal with furries who rebel against the new policy demanding to be treated the same as humans. They march in the streets, calling to end the Oceanice Republic's prejudice toward the furry community. 

.S.S.E. Office stepping out from his car, he looked at his comrades and called out troops to step in. 

[u].S.S.E. Office[/u] These beast wants to show respect to us, we will give them that respect. Our order is to shoot them when they come here. Make sure no one doesnt leaves in sight. 

He lit his cigarettes, looking anxious at the time. 
 
Rain pattered lightly against the pavement as the city lights flickered in the mist. The protest ahead burned with chants, signs raised high We Are Equal!  Fur is Not a Crime!  Stop the Decree!
From behind the tinted window of an armored black cruiser, the S.S.E. Officer took a slow drag of his cigarette. Smoke curled into the humid night as he gave the nod. The armored boots of his squad began to step forward in formation, sleek, black-clad, faceless beneath their visors.

[u]S.S.E. Officer[/u]
No mercy. No witness. No retreat.

He turned to his second-in-command, a younger officer with hesitation in his eyes.

[u]Second Officer[/u]
Sir theyre unarmed. Many of them are just kids citizens. We were told only to disperse
The Officer grabbed him by the collar, whispering with quiet fury*

[u]S.S.E. Officer[/u]
They chose rebellion. And rebellion is infection. You cut infection out. Now follow your order... or join them.

As the squad advanced toward the main boulevard, the sound of chanting turned into screams. Barricades were lit. Protesters threw bottles, makeshift smokescreens  but they were met with flashbangs and rubber bullets, and soon, live rounds.

One furry activist, a young lion anthropomorphic. Stood on a car roof with a megaphone
Activist, roaring in the streets

WE ARE OCEANICIAN! NO MORE CHAINS! THIS STREETS ARE OURS!

A red dot found his chest*

[u]S.S.E. Officer[/u]
He wants to be seen? Make him history.

The lion protestor stood tall atop the hood of the burned out vehicle, defiant, blood trickling down his brow, the megaphone still in his hand. Around him, dozens of protesters of canine, feline, scaled, and feathered gathered behind makeshift barricades of overturned benches and dumpsters. Their chants were fading, replaced with breathless fear.

Across the street, the S.S.E. Officer raised his hand and then lowered it slowly, drawing his pistol with theatrical flair.

He smirked*

[u]S.S.E. Officer[/u]
Foolish beast now Ill make you see why we humans are at the top of the chain.
 FIRE!

[b]The night erupted[/b]
Gunfire thundered like a storm breaking loose. Muzzle flashes lit up the darkened boulevard in flashes of orange and white. The lion protestor was thrown backward by the force of the bullets  his body fell limp onto the car roof, the megaphone clattering to the asphalt below with a hollow thud.

Screams rang out. Chaos surged like a tidal wave. Protesters scattered. Some ran. Some froze. Some fought.

A young canine hybrid hurled a Molotov, lighting one of the S.S.E. transports on fire. But it was a spark against the storm.

One of the S.S.E. soldiers hesitated, watching a frightened child huddled behind a mailbox, claws over her ears.

Second Officer whispering*
Sir, were shooting civilians this isnt suppression. This is a purge.

S.S.E. Officer coldly*
Good. Make it clean.

He blew another puff of smoke into the air, watching the flames reflect in the wet pavement like dancing ghosts.

The smoke still lingered in the air. Fires crackled down the boulevard. The screams had died, replaced by the soft patter of rain and distant sirens. A young leopard girl, no older than six, trembled behind a rusting mailbox, blood splattered on her fur. Her wide eyes stared at two mangled bodies on the ground lay her mother and father, unrecognizable from gunfire. Their limbs twisted, their bodies limp, like broken dolls thrown into the gutter.

A black-armored S.S.E. soldier approached, eyes cold behind his visor. He raised his Maschinengewehr 42, locking onto the child. The gun clicked. She whimpered.
But just as he steadied his aim.

Hold your fire!

 A sharp voice broke through. The Second Officer, Alexa Herman, rushed in and slammed the barrel down. The soldier looked at him in confusion but lowered his weapon.
Alexa stared at the child, then at her parents.

He froze.

The look on the mother's face, mouth agape, blood smeared over fur, hit him like a ghost from his past. He took a knee before the child and whispered, Its alright... youre safe now.
He scooped the leopard girl into his arms and hurried away from the massacre. He tucked her into the back seat of his personal car, wrapping his coat around her tiny, shivering body.

[b]Inside the Armored Car[/b]

Alexa marched to his commander, the S.S.E. Officer, now seated in his armored vehicle, smoking again, staring dead-eyed into the mirror.

[u]Alexa[/u]
Why did you do that? They were civilians. Families. That child she was hiding behind her parents corpses.
The Officer didnt turn. Just exhaled.

[u]S.S.E. Officer[/u]
You dont know what they took from me. My wife my little girl both torn apart by a pack of furries. They called it self-defense. My family never stood a chance. So nono sympathy from me. They want to call themselves equal? Let them burn equally.
He finally turned to Alexa, eyes empty.

[u]S.S.E. Officer[/u]
You dont see beasts. I do.
Alexa clenched his fists but said nothing. That rage wasnt justice. It was grief, twisted into genocide.

[b]That Night | Alexas Apartment[/b]

The city skyline blinked through the window. Alexa opened a door, a soft pink-lit room, untouched for years. Stuffed animals lined the shelves. A photo frame stood on the dresser.

[u]Alexa[/u]
This was my little sisters room. She died young cancer. She was about your age.
He gently placed the young leopard on the bed, handing her a pair of soft, silk pajamas.

[u]Alexa[/u]
Its okay if you cant speak. Youve been through hell. Youll be safe here. My name is Alexa. Alexa Herman.
The girls eyes wandered to the dresser. She saw the photo of Alexa as a boy, standing next to his sister. But her gaze narrowed. She tilted her head and whispered, finally speaking for the first time

[u]Leopard Girl softly[/u]
He... looks like the leader... from the news.

Alexa froze*
He turned toward the frame, lips trembling.

[u]Alexa[/u]
That... thats my father.
He looked away.

[u]Alexa whispers*[/u]
This used to be her room. And I... I dont want to remember that day.
He wiped his face, his voice cracking.

[u]Alexa[/u]
You should get some sleep.
He gently closed the door behind him.

[b]Later|In the Living Room[/b]

His phone buzzed*
 Caller ID (Father  President Vanklyis Adelais Herman)

He hesitated, then answered.

[u]President Herman in calm and authoritative*[/u]
Alexa. Status report. How did the orders go? Any complications?

Alexa stared through the glass window at the burning city.

He didnt answer right away.

His eyes, once full of duty, now held something else.

Doubt.

[quote=dhornaper;59820260]General Fereydun surveys some the build up of his eastern forces in person when he is interrupted by a phone call from the Cabinet Secretary.

"Sir, Hydronia has informed us that they are halting supply of food and uranium to us."

"They're either upset at the coup or the planned military exercises, in either case, they'll get over it eventually. Inform them in turn that aluminium shipments will resume when their shipments resume and that we intend to have friendly relations with Hydronia."

"Yes, sir."

With the conversation over, he turns to his staff. "Get all units built up here in seven days and then immediately put them through hell for three more days. I want them exhausted and spent by the end of the exercises."[/quote]

General Fereydun watches the last day of the military exercises unfold with some impatience. He taps his foot as he watches some of his men from his seat on a nearby hill. He abruptly says "take notes" to the chief of staff before beginning his observations.

"From what I've seen, the men know cover and concealment well, they can exploit the variations of the earth to hide and take cover and are sufficiently dispersed.

The first problem I see is that small units have trouble maneuvering well because their ability to provide covering fire is weak. The men need to be trained to judge their next position better, see their neighbour's next position, and provide enough covering fire. The time and effects of crossing open ground between positions then is lessened.

The next is where things will get difficult. The infantry work well with the artillery but communication on target locations isn't good enough. The artillery can do suppressive fire on static targets but changing to a new target is slow and accuracy of hitting moving targets poor.

The infantry works well with mechanised units but again, it's the artillery.

Now, you'll need to ask the air staff chief on problems with the air force since that's not my expertise. I want you and him to attend the other planned exercises across the country and watch for the same issues spotted here. I'm heading back to Shar to reorganise the government and draft reforms from what I've spotted here."

With his observations complete, he leaves for Shar as the exercises wind down.
